children: Australian stocks fell 26 points, or 0.3%, to 8,883 in early trade on Monday, reversing recent gains as tech, non-energy minerals, and healthcare stocks fell.

Caution prevailed ahead of Tuesday’s Reserve Bank interest rate decision, with the central bank expected to raise its cash rate for the fifth time this year to 4.85% amid persistent inflationary pressure.
In key trading partner China, official data showed an unexpected drop in manufacturing during October, partly reflecting the impact of the Golden Week break.
However, losses were capped by fresh data showing a September rebound in Australia's building permits, driven by a recovery in private-sector dwellings excl. houses.
In the U.S., stock futures strengthened ahead of further corporate earnings, jobs data, and the midterm elections.
BHP Group fell 1.1% while Rio Tinto lost 1.4%.
Gold miners like Northern Star (-3.9%) and Evolution Mining (-2.5%) also slipped.
In contrast, the four major banks rose between 0.2% and 1.6%.

title: Australian Shares Start Week Lower as RBA Decision Looms
